messages:
maria: quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for docs-as-contract for quickstarts + launch AC. want to lock acceptance criteria and the minimal examples we ship with the quickstart. goal: docs = testable spec so we can sign off without last-minute scope creep.

simon: +1. can we scope the initial quickstart to a single language and 2 model types? engineering capacity is tight this sprint.

lee: from devex POV we should include an end-to-end sample that runs locally and uses the hosted API. acceptance criteria should include a runnable example with documented env vars.

anya: design note — keep screenshots out of the quickstart itself, link to a separate style doc. quickstarts should be CLI-first, then snackable UI plug.

ben: customer asks: enterprise customers want a dedicated capacity example and a checklist for security review. can we add a short node/python snippet that highlights auth + KMS integration?

maria: proposed MVP AC: 1) Quickstart includes 1 language (python), 2 model variants (small & quantized medium), 3) runnable instructions that boot a sample app in <10 minutes, 4) CI test that runs the sample and verifies expected output, 5) security checklist + link to Private deployment notes.

simon: suggest reducing to 1 model variant (quantized medium) for MVP so we can ship this sprint; we can add the small model later.

lee: tradeoff accepted if we make the CI test robust. sample CI job must assert two things: process returns 200 and output contains the example "status: ok" token. i'll draft the CI snippet.

maria: here's an example AC snippet i want in the PRD so reviewers have something concrete:

```
Acceptance Criteria: Quickstart v1
- Setup: user can follow README and run `./start.sh` with only the provided free credits env var.
- Functionality: sample generates text for prompt "Hello, Redwood" and returns a JSON with field `result` that contains at least 3 tokens.
- Verification: CI job `quickstart-e2e` runs `curl` against local server and fails if \"result\" not present.
- Docs-as-spec: README contains exact command outputs for happy-path and one documented error case (401 when API key invalid).
```

anya: we need an edge-case AC: what happens when model is rate-limited -> quickstart should show the fallback message and a link to docs. include sample output for 429.

ben: customer edge-case: network latency >3s. can the quickstart include a section on retry/backoff example? that'll be helpful for adoption.

simon: code-level note — we must not commit real API keys in examples. use placeholders + env var check that errors loudly if missing. i'll add a linter rule to CI to assert no key-like strings in repo.

maria: negotiation: scope shipped this sprint = python quickstart, quantized-medium model, CI e2e verifying happy-path + 401 + 429 example outputs, security checklist link. not shipping node snippet or dedicated capacity example yet.

lee: ok. i'll own the CI and sample app. ETA: EOD Thu for draft PR.

anya: i'll write the example outputs and UX copy for errors. ETA: tomorrow morning.

ben: i'll craft a short addendum for enterprise customers explaining Dedicated and Private mapping, to be linked from the quickstart.

maria: i'll update the PRD and add acceptance tests as checklist items. tagging reviewers: @simon @lee @anya @ben. once PRD has ACs as tests we treat docs review as release gating.

deploy-bot: reminder: create a draft PR in repo `redwood/quickstarts` with branch `docs-contract/quickstart-v1` when initial commit is pushed.

simon: fine with treating docs as gating tests. small ask — add a follow-up ticket to add node example in next sprint.

maria: noted; i'll create follow-up ticket and link in PR. action items: lee -> CI + sample app, anya -> outputs & copy, ben -> enterprise addendum, simon -> linter rule, maria -> PRD + create follow-up ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
